cells.scene: A fair-minded manager attentively listens to suggestions from several workers and welcomes their ideas with an open gesture.
An adult first chooses a blue hat, then immediately turns toward a red hat, abandoned choices on a chair and indecisive expression.
A diligent adult continues carefully cleaning a stubborn stain after many attempts, focused posture and repeated worn cleaning cloths.
A hopeful buyer discovers that a supposedly fine antique vase is only a cheap cracked copy, disappointed expression.

prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE SQUARE 2x2 atlas with four equal square cells for an adult vocabulary app. Attached image is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: restrained ink-and-watercolor educational illustrations, clear dark blue-charcoal outlines, pale blue wash, small warm natural color accents. Pure WHITE opaque background. Central 75% of each quadrant contains its subject with generous margins. Nothing crosses midlines. Leave horizontal 45–55% and vertical 47–53% center bands EMPTY WHITE. Natural human anatomy, recognizable objects, clear 320px silhouettes, restrained detail, no elaborate environment. NO captions, labels, writing, borders, grid lines, watermarks or logos. Only symbols or numerals explicitly requested in a cell are allowed. Meanings are guidance; never write them. Row-major fixed order. FOUR CELLS:
TOP LEFT — enlightened (a.开明的，教化的): A fair-minded manager attentively listens to suggestions from several workers and welcomes their ideas with an open gesture.
TOP RIGHT — fickleness (n.变化无常): An adult first chooses a blue hat, then immediately turns toward a red hat, abandoned choices on a chair and indecisive expression.
BOTTOM LEFT — unrelenting (a.不屈不挠的，不松懈的): A diligent adult continues carefully cleaning a stubborn stain after many attempts, focused posture and repeated worn cleaning cloths.
BOTTOM RIGHT — disillusion (v.使幻想破灭): A hopeful buyer discovers that a supposedly fine antique vase is only a cheap cracked copy, disappointed expression.
CRITICAL SAFE COMPOSITION: Make subjects SMALLER than the style reference. Every subject fits within central 65% of its own quadrant, with large 20% white margins on all sides. Bottom-row subjects including heads and thought bubbles begin BELOW 58% of entire canvas height; top subjects end ABOVE 42%. Keep central horizontal 42–58% totally blank white. No head, limb, object or speech bubble crosses either exact 50% midline.
review_notes: All four cells visually reviewed. Enlightened manager listening, persistent cleaning, and disappointed vase buyer are semantically accurate and contained. Fickleness has an impossible third hand while comparing hats; this cell rejected and superseded by repair-late-002.
